answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it directly reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, addressing both value and sustainability. Memory 44 provides strong evidence through improved enterprise conversion and pipeline quality, though realized revenue and durability are omitted. Memories 31 and 86 show activation or adoption gains, with memory 31 noting durability, but neither connects those gains to qualified revenue. Memory 73 reports acquisition and revenue lift in the currently relevant price-sensitive SMB segment, but omits margins, retention, discount dependence, and long-term durability. Memory 91 is weakest because it establishes only short-term engagement and first-action gains, without evidence of revenue quality, retention, or sustained impact.
